carried.grounds: `spec.origin and spec.has_location` vs `or` differ only on (bool(origin), has_location) = (T,F) or (F,T). Every spec given to inside() (single call at 807) comes from PathFinder.find_spec (resolve at 802/804, the __main__ lookup at 806); under -I -S sys.path_hooks is exactly zipimporter + FileFinder (printed by my spec_pairs.py). A PathFinder spec is either spec_from_file_location (origin=location and _set_fileattr=True set together -> (T,T); also for zipimporter, which goes spec_from_loader -> spec_from_file_location because it has get_filename) or a namespace portion ModuleSpec(name, None) whose origin PathFinder.find_spec sets to None (CPython >= 3.7; requires-python >= 3.11) -> (F,F). (T,F) is only produced by spec_from_loader for loaders without get_filename (built-in/frozen importers), which PathFinder never consults; (F,T) cannot be built. Corroboration (not the proof): spec_pairs.py on 3.14.7 under -I -S over 291 specs (stdlib roots incl. __pycache__ dirs, a tree with regular, namespace, empty dir, module, sourceless .pyc, and a zip with module, package and namespace): 287 (T,T), 4 (F,F), 0 mixed.

carried.grounds: HARNESS L29 False->True is `said.acquire(blocking=False)` -> `blocking=True` in conclude(), reached only from the daemon Timer built in deadline() (cli_invocation.py:718-720; timer is never joined or cancelled). `said` (703) is acquired at 711 (settle, non-blocking) and 714 (conclude) and never released anywhere in the script, so after the first successful acquire it stays held for the life of the process. A blocking acquire on a free lock returns at once and writes RESULT/END exactly like the non-blocking one; on a held lock the non-blocking call returns without writing and the blocking call never returns and therefore never writes: protocol file, RESULT winner, exit status identical. The one difference is a parked daemon thread, which interpreter exit does not wait for (measured with park.py under python -I -S 3.14.7: wrote [] in both, exit 0.46 s vs 0.47 s, only 'timer alive' differs). No reader sees a thread of another process.
